We need to find a permanent home for the falcosecurity-libs and falcosecurity-libs-devel RPMs.
I originally thought that we could put them in https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark-development-libraries but it probably makes more sense to put them on the Wireshark download servers, since Stratoshark requires the falcosecurity-libs RPM.

+# The note above about generating a warning because dumpcap is listed twice
+# applies here as well.
+# The minimum set of capabibilities we need for syscall capture are
+# CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_SYS_RESOURCE, CAP_BPF, and CAP_PERFMON.
+# However, Docker doesn't support CAP_BPF and CAP_PERFMON so we use
+# CAP_SYS_ADMIN instead.
+# https://falco.org/docs/setup/container/#docker-least-privileged-modern-ebpf
+%if %{use_stratoshark_group} && %{setuid_falcodump}
+# Setuid but only executable by members of the 'stratoshark' group

+# Setcap but only executable by members of the 'stratoshark' group

+%if %{setuid_falcodump}

+%else

+%endif

commits_data.title: packaging: Add Stratoshark to the RPM .spec
commits_data.message:
packaging: Add Stratoshark to the RPM .spec

Add a "stratoshark" subpackage to our RPM .spec. Include support for a
"stratoshark" group, which has permissions to capture system calls
locally.

Enable Stratoshark and falcodump in the Fedora and Rocky Linux jobs.
